concerns.text: T028 (LOO Jackknife loop) is marked [P] (parallel-safe). However, the task description implies a sequential accumulation of results ('N iterations... removing one model at a time') and T029b requires comparing each LOO subsample to the 'full ensemble results'. If T028 runs in parallel, the 'full ensemble' baseline must be pre-computed and immutable. The current task list does not explicitly mandate a 'Compute Full Ensemble Baseline' task *before* T028, creating a race condition where parallel workers might attempt to read a baseline that hasn't been finalized or is being modified by the same phase's logic.

T024 (Save eigenvalues/eigenfunctions) is marked [X] (complete) but T028 (LOO loop) and T029 (Procrustes alignment) depend on these artifacts. The task list shows T024 as complete, yet the 'Re-plan' section and T023/T024 status in the text indicate these artifacts are missing. This creates a semantic ordering violation: downstream tasks (T028+) are listed as ready to execute or complete, but their required producer tasks (T024) are effectively incomplete or missing in the actual state, blocking the data flow.

T018 (Save processed B-spline coefficients) is marked [ ] (incomplete) but T021 (Load B-spline coefficients for fPCA) is marked [X] (complete). This is a direct producer-consumer violation: the consumer task (T021) claims to be done before the producer task (T018) that generates its input artifact is finished. T021 cannot logically precede T018.

T004 (Setup data directory structure) is listed in Phase 2, but T001a (Create root directory and subdirectories) in Phase 1 already covers 'data/' subdirectories. T004 appears to be a redundant re-creation of the directory structure. While not a hard ordering violation, it creates confusion in the dependency graph regarding when the 'data/processed' directory is actually available for T018/T024.
